paper.title_en: Singularity-free anisotropic models of compact stars via gravitational decoupling in general relativity
paper.abstract_en: This research develops two new anisotropic solutions by applying the minimal geometric deformation approach in the context of Einstein's gravitational theory. We begin with the assumption of a static spherical system containing the anisotropic fluid which is regarded as the original source. A new source is then added, connected gravitationally to the original fluid distribution. After computing the field equations, the use of a transformation on the radial component yields two independent systems of equations. These are solved independently using distinct constraints, resulting in novel solutions. In order to determine the unknowns in internal solutions, we use boundary conditions. We then test the given solutions by performing a graphical analysis using the known masses and radii of two stars, namely LMC X-4 and SAX J1808.4-3658. Our analysis demonstrates that both compact stellar models meet all actual criteria for specific values of decoupling parameter.
